title: Long comfortable lives fooled them into thinking they were right.
subtitle: Ease that lasts can feel like approval
then: Allah explains that they were {trap}deceived by their luxuries and the long life they had been given{/trap}, so they believed they were following something good. He asks if they do not see the land being reduced from its edges. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said this meant {idea}the victory of Islam over disbelief{/idea}.
now: Business is good, the family is healthy, nothing bad has happened in years. {trap}It is tempting to read that as a sign you're on the right path.{/trap} {idea}Ease is a gift and a respite, not a certificate.{/idea}
old: Things going well for me means I am doing fine with Allah.
new: A long good stretch is a respite to use, not proof that I am right.
try: In a good season, ask yourself one honest question: what am I neglecting while it's easy?

title: I only warn you by revelation, but the deaf hear nothing.
subtitle: A warning works only on ears willing to hear
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say he only conveys {idea}what Allah reveals to him{/idea}. The tafsir says this {trap}is of no benefit to the one whose hearing and heart are sealed{/trap}. The deaf will not hear the call, even when warned.
now: Your mother has told you about the late nights a dozen times. You hear the words and tune them out before she finishes. {trap}That is a kind of deafness.{/trap} {idea}Ears can work while the heart refuses.{/idea}
old: If the message were clearer, I would act on it.
new: Most warnings are clear enough. What matters is whether I let myself hear.
try: Think of one reminder you hear often and tune out. Listen to it fully once today.

title: One whiff of His punishment, and they would confess.
subtitle: How quickly bravado breaks
then: The mockers asked for the punishment boldly. The tafsir says that {trap}if they were touched by even the slightest of it{/trap}, they would confess their sins and admit {idea}they had wronged themselves{/idea}. Their confidence was only skin deep.
now: You are confident about skipping the check-up, until one sharp chest pain at the gym. {trap}Then you promise everything.{/trap} {idea}Better to admit it now, by choice, while it can still change your life.{/idea}
old: I am fine as I am. I don't need to change.
new: My confidence may be thinner than I think. Better to turn back by choice.
try: Admit one fault to Allah today, before anything forces you to.

title: Scales of justice: not even a mustard seed is lost.
subtitle: Every deed is weighed, and no one is wronged
then: Most scholars say it is one Balance, plural to reflect how many deeds are weighed. A companion once told the Prophet ﷺ he hit and insulted his servants. The Prophet ﷺ explained that {trap}any punishment beyond what they deserved would be taken from him{/trap}. The man wept and {reward}set them all free{/reward}.
now: The sharp reply to your child after a long shift. The extra effort no one at work noticed. {idea}Both are on the scale.{/idea} {reward}Two light phrases, SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil 'Azim, are heavy there.{/reward}
old: Small things I do and say don't really count.
new: Even a mustard seed of good or harm will be weighed. Nothing is wasted.
try: Say SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil 'Azim ten times today.

title: Musa and Harun were given the Criterion, a light and a reminder.
subtitle: Scripture that separates truth from falsehood

row.title: a light
sub: fills the heart, shows the way

then: The tafsir notes Allah often mentions Musa and Muhammad ﷺ together, and their Books together. Qatadah said the Criterion was the Tawrah, {idea}how Allah differentiated between truth and falsehood{/idea}. The heavenly Books also bring {reward}what fills the heart with light, guidance, and repentance{/reward}.
now: You face a choice at work where everyone says it's fine, and you're not sure. {idea}Guidance is a criterion: it helps you tell right from wrong{/idea} when the crowd blurs it. {reward}And it lights you from inside.{/reward}
old: Scripture is a list of rules to follow.
new: Scripture is a light that helps me see what is true when things blur.
try: Bring one unclear choice to the Quran today. Look up what it says about it.

title: They fear their Lord unseen and are wary of the Hour.
subtitle: Who the reminder actually reaches
then: The verse describes those who benefit from the reminder: they {idea}fear their Lord in the unseen{/idea} and are afraid of the Hour. The tafsir links it to another verse: {reward}theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward{/reward}.
now: The hotel room on a work trip. The browser with no one looking. The office after everyone has gone. {idea}What you do there is what you really believe.{/idea} {reward}That private moment is where forgiveness is earned.{/reward}
old: I behave well because people know me.
new: Real faith shows when no one is watching but Allah.
try: In one private moment today, choose the better thing because only He sees.

title: This is a blessed reminder. Will you deny it?
subtitle: The Quran as blessing, clear and close at hand
then: After Musa's Book, Allah points to the Quran: {reward}a blessed reminder He has sent down{/reward}. The tafsir says falsehood cannot approach it. Then the question: {trap}will you deny it{/trap}, when it is the utmost in clarity and truth?
now: You have an app with the full Quran on your phone, next to forty others you open daily. {trap}Not denying it, exactly. Just not opening it.{/trap} {reward}Blessing sits there waiting.{/reward}
old: I already know what the Quran says, more or less.
new: The Quran is a blessing sent to me. Ignoring it is a quiet kind of denial.
try: Move the Quran app to your home screen and open it once today.

title: Ibrahim was guided early, and Allah knew him well.
subtitle: Guidance given to a young man who was worthy of it
then: Allah {idea}inspired Ibrahim with truth from an early age{/idea}, with proof against his people. The tafsir says {reward}he was worthy of that{/reward}, and Allah was well acquainted with him. The surah now turns to the stories of the prophets.
now: Your teenager asks hard questions about God over dinner. You think, they're too young to get it. {idea}Ibrahim saw clearly as a young man.{/idea} {reward}Young hearts can be the most honest.{/reward}
old: Serious faith is for when you are older.
new: Guidance can come early. Allah knows who is ready for it.
try: Ask a young person in your family what they think about Allah, and listen.

title: What are these statues you sit so devoted to?
subtitle: A young man questioning what everyone takes for granted
then: This was the guidance Ibrahim had in his youth: {idea}his denunciation of his people's worship of idols{/idea} instead of Allah. He asked his own father and people {trap}what these images were that they worshipped with such devotion{/trap}.
now: Look at what your family gives hours to: the TV schedule, the status, what the neighbours think. {trap}Some things get devotion just because they are always there.{/trap} {idea}A simple question can break the spell.{/idea}
old: Everyone around me is devoted to these things, so they must matter.
new: Devotion should have a reason. It is fair to ask what I am devoted to.
try: Ask yourself: what got most of my attention this week? Is it worth that?

title: Their only answer: our fathers did it.
subtitle: Tradition offered in place of evidence
then: Asked what the idols were, his people answered: {trap}we found our fathers worshipping them{/trap}. The tafsir notes {idea}they had no other evidence{/idea} apart from the misguided actions of their forefathers.
now: We have always done the wedding this way. We always shout in arguments. We always keep money matters secret. {trap}Always is not a reason.{/trap} {idea}Keep what is good; question what is only habit.{/idea}
old: This is how my family has always done it.
new: That something was inherited does not make it right. I can check it.
try: Pick one family habit and ask honestly whether it pleases Allah.

title: You and your fathers were plainly wrong.
subtitle: Error does not become right with age
then: Ibrahim answered that speaking to their fathers {idea}would be the same as speaking to them{/idea}. The tafsir paraphrases: {trap}both you and they are misguided{/trap} and not on any straight path. Pointing to the past did not move the question.
now: You love your grandparents. You also know one of their habits was unfair to someone. {idea}You can honour people and still not repeat their mistake.{/idea} {reward}That is often the kindest thing for the next generation.{/reward}
old: Saying my elders were wrong would be disrespectful.
new: I can respect those before me and still say a wrong was wrong.
try: Choose one inherited mistake you will not pass on, and make dua for the ones before you.

title: Are you serious, or just playing?
subtitle: When the truth is so unfamiliar it sounds like a joke
then: When Ibrahim questioned their intelligence and belittled their gods, they asked: {trap}are you speaking in jest or telling the truth?{/trap} The tafsir adds their reason: {idea}we have never heard such a thing before{/idea}.
now: A friend suggests you give up the extra job and spend evenings with your kids. {trap}It sounds ridiculous because no one you know does it.{/trap} {idea}Unfamiliar is not the same as wrong.{/idea}
old: If I have never heard it before, it is probably not serious.
new: Truth can sound strange just because I have not heard it. That is not a reason to laugh it off.
try: Take one idea you dismissed as strange this week and think about it seriously for five minutes.

title: Your Lord made the heavens and earth, and I bear witness.
subtitle: Ibrahim's clear answer: the Creator is the Lord
then: Ibrahim was not joking. He said {idea}your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them{/idea}. The tafsir adds that He initiated their creation and is the Creator of all things. And Ibrahim said: {reward}I bear witness{/reward} that there is no god other than Him.
now: Someone at the table asks, half laughing, if you actually believe all this. You can mumble, or you can say plainly what you believe, kindly. {reward}Ibrahim simply testified.{/reward}
old: I keep my beliefs quiet so no one thinks I am strange.
new: I can calmly say what I believe. The Creator is my Lord, and I testify to it.
try: If faith comes up in conversation today, say one clear, kind sentence about what you believe.
